category_title: Third-grade male with EBD exhibiting aggressive behavior and a punishment-obedience moral orientation
minimal_context: Henry is participating in a one-on-one interview and is asked to recall the names of characters immediately after hearing a story.
dialogue:
TUTOR: I just finished reading the first story to you. Can you tell me the names of the characters we just heard about?

STUDENT: I liked the story and I want to answer, but I forgot what they were called.

TUTOR: Just try your best to think about it.

STUDENT: Yes, ma'am. I know one boy broke a lot of cups, but I don't know his name.

TUTOR: Keep trying to remember.

STUDENT: I'm sorry, I just can't remember their names at all from hearing it that one time.

options.A: Ask the student to justify their answers about the story characters.
options.B: Read the story aloud to the student for a second time.
options.C: Use a physical prop to signal role-switching and perform monologues as the story characters.
options.D: Ask 'Is it possible' questions (e.g., 'Is it possible to remember the names?').
